```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
model_name <- "Singh_2019_trastuzumab_vc_mmae_mouse_qsp"
mod <- modellib(model_name)
meta <- {
  fun <- readModelDb(model_name)
  if (is.function(fun)) fun() else fun
}
```

* Citation: `r meta$reference`
* Description: `r meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics11020098>

Singh, Guo, Verma, Wong and Shah (2019) extended their single-cell
pharmacokinetic model of the HER2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate
trastuzumab-vc-MMAE (T-vc-MMAE) to tumor-bearing mice. The model (Figure 1 and
Equations 1-23 of the paper) joins four layers:

* **plasma PK**: a two-compartment ADC model with linear catabolic clearance and
  first-order non-specific deconjugation, which also lowers the average
  drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR); unconjugated MMAE is formed by both pathways and
  has its own two-compartment disposition;
* **tumor distribution**: vascular (Krogh cylinder) and surface exchange of ADC
  and MMAE between plasma and the tumor extracellular space, with the tumor
  radius recomputed from the current tumor volume;
* **single-cell disposition**: HER2 binding, internalization and lysosomal
  degradation of the ADC, MMAE influx/efflux and binding to tubulin, all in
  molecules per average tumor cell and diluted at the tumor growth rate;
* **cell-level killing**: tubulin occupancy drives a sigmoid kill rate that moves
  proliferating tumor volume into a three-stage death transit chain; dying
  cells return their ADC and MMAE content to the tumor extracellular space.

The plasma PK parameters were estimated first, the tumor and cell parameters
were fixed from the literature except the in-vivo HER2 receptor counts, and the
kill parameters were then estimated from the tumor growth inhibition (TGI) data
of both xenografts with one shared set of values. The cell line is selected by
`CELLLINE_NCIN87` (1 = NCI-N87, 0 = GFP-MCF7).

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- meta$population
tibble::tibble(
  Field = names(pop),
  Value = vapply(pop, function(x) paste(as.character(x), collapse = "; "), character(1))
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Male SCID mice (NOD.CB17-Prkdcscid/J, Jackson Laboratory) were implanted at
8 weeks with about 10 million NCI-N87 or GFP-MCF7 cells (Section 2.3). Eighteen
mice (9 per tumor line, tumors ~500 mm^3) received a single 10 mg/kg IV dose for
plasma and tumor PK with terminal sampling at 1, 3 and 7 days (Section 2.5);
56 mice (7 per arm, tumors ~350-400 mm^3) entered the TGI study at 0, 3, 5 or
10 mg/kg (GFP-MCF7) and 0, 1, 3 or 10 mg/kg (N87) (Section 2.6). The paper does
not report body weights.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl`, `lq` | 0.033, 0.0585 L/day/kg | Table 1 (CLADC, CLDADC) |
| `lvc`, `lvp` | 0.084, 0.051 L/kg | Table 1 (V1ADC, V2ADC) |
| `lkdec` | 0.323 1/day | Table 1 (KdecP) |
| `dar0` | 4 | Section 2.2 ('average DAR of ~4'); initial condition of Eq 7 |
| `lcl_mmae`, `lq_mmae` | 18.40, 1.84 L/day/kg | Table 1 (CLDrug, CLDDrug, from ref 11) |
| `lvc_mmae`, `lvp_mmae` | 0.136, 0.523 L/kg | Table 1 (V1Drug, V2Drug, from ref 11) |
| `rcap`, `rkrogh` | 8.0, 75.0 um | Table 1 |
| `perm`, `perm_mmae` | 334, 21000 um/day | Table 1 (PADC, PDrug) |
| `dif`, `dif_mmae` | 0.022, 0.25 cm^2/day | Table 1 (DADC, DDrug) |
| `eps`, `eps_mmae` | 0.24, 0.44 | Table 1 (tumor void fractions) |
| `kon`, `koff` | 0.03 1/nM/h, 0.014 1/h | Table 1 (KonADC, KoffADC) |
| `kint`, `kdeg` | 0.11, 0.353 1/h | Table 1 (KintADC, KdegADC) |
| `kon_tub`, `koff_tub` | 0.0183 1/nM/h, 0.545 1/h | Table 1 (KonTub, KoffTub) |
| `tub_tot` | 65 nM | Table 1 (Tubtot) |
| `kin_mmae`, `kout_mmae` | 8.33, 0.046 1/h | Table 1 (KinDrug, KoutDrug) |
| `vcell_n87`, `vcell_mcf7` | 3.12, 8.14 pL | Singh and Shah 2017 (Drug Metab Dispos 45:1120), Table 2 |
| SF (in `model()`) | 10^9 / 6.023e23 nmol per molecule | Singh and Shah 2017, Table 2 |
| `lag_n87`, `lag_mcf7` | 185,000, 22,400 receptors/cell | Table 1 (AgN87ex, AgMCF7ex) |
| `ldt_n87`, `ldt_mcf7` | 13.5, 10.6 day | Table 1 (DTN87, DTMCF7) |
| `lkmax`, `lkc50` | 1.03 1/day, 96.8 % | Table 1 (Kmax, KC50) |
| `ltau`, `lhill` | 2.03 day, 15.02 | Table 1 (tau, gamma) |
| `etalkmax`, `etaltau` | omega 0.1016, 0.194 | Table 1 (IIVKmax 10.16 %, IIVtau 19.4 %) |
| `propSd`, `propSd_tumor_volume` | 0 (fixed) | not reported |
| Tumor growth, radius | Eqs 1-2, 15 | Section 2.7.3 |
| Plasma ADC, MMAE, DAR | Eqs 3-7 | Section 2.7.3 |
| Tumor extracellular ADC, MMAE | Eqs 22-23 (supersede Eqs 8-9) | Section 2.7.5 |
| Single-cell states | Eqs 10-13 | Section 2.7.3 |
| Tubulin occupancy, kill, transit | Eqs 14, 16-21 | Sections 2.7.4-2.7.5 |
| Cells per tumor volume | 10^8 cells/g = 10^5 cells/mm^3 | Section 2.7.3; factor 10^5 in Eqs 22-23 |
| Deconjugated antibody in plasma | `mab_central`, `mab_peripheral` | reconstructed from Figure 4A (see deviations) |

# Simulation setup

Doses are entered in nmol of antibody. The paper reports neither body weight
nor the molecular weight of the ADC, so this vignette uses a 25 g mouse and
150,000 g/mol (the molecular weight of an IgG1 carrying about four vc-MMAE
drug-linkers); 10 mg/kg is then 1.67 nmol.

```{r helpers}
wt <- 0.025 # kg
mw_adc <- 150000 # g/mol
dose_nmol <- function(mgkg) mgkg * wt * 1e6 / mw_adc

# Two declared endpoints (Cc and tumor_volume): observation rows carry dvid = 1
# and every output column comes back on each row.
make_events <- function(mgkg, n87, tv0, times, n_id = 1L) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_nmol(mgkg), cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(times)
  if (n_id > 1L) ev <- rxode2::et(ev, id = seq_len(n_id))
  d <- as.data.frame(ev)
  d$dvid <- ifelse(d$evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_)
  d$CELLLINE_NCIN87 <- n87
  d$TUM_VOL <- tv0
  d$WT <- wt
  d
}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
solve_typ <- function(mgkg, n87, tv0, times) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, make_events(mgkg, n87, tv0, times),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  ))
}
line_lab <- function(n87) ifelse(n87 == 1, "N87", "GFP-MCF7")
```

# Plasma and tumor PK after 10 mg/kg (Figure 4)

```{r pk-sim}
pk_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 7, by = 0.05), 10 / 1440)))
pk <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_typ(10, 0, 500, pk_times) |> dplyr::mutate(line = "GFP-MCF7"),
  solve_typ(10, 1, 500, pk_times) |> dplyr::mutate(line = "N87")
)
pk_long <- pk |>
  dplyr::select(line, time,
    `Total trastuzumab` = Cc,
    `Total MMAE` = plasma_total_mmae,
    `Unconjugated MMAE` = plasma_free_mmae
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(line, time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc")
```

```{r fig4a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4A of Singh 2019: plasma total trastuzumab, total MMAE and unconjugated MMAE after a single 10 mg/kg IV dose (typical values). Points are the paper's fitted lines at 0, 3 and 7 days, digitized by the maintainers."}
fig4a_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~time, ~conc,
  "Total trastuzumab", 0, 740, "Total trastuzumab", 3, 214, "Total trastuzumab", 7, 82,
  "Total MMAE", 0, 2900, "Total MMAE", 3, 162, "Total MMAE", 7, 10.5,
  "Unconjugated MMAE", 0, 10.5, "Unconjugated MMAE", 3, 0.58, "Unconjugated MMAE", 7, 0.034
)
ggplot(pk_long |> dplyr::filter(conc > 0), aes(time, conc, colour = analyte)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = line)) +
  geom_point(data = fig4a_ref, size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Concentration (nM)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig4a-check}
ref_at <- fig4a_ref |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(3, 7)) |>
  dplyr::rename(paper = conc)
ratio <- pk_long |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(3, 7)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(ref_at, by = c("analyte", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = conc / paper)
ratio |>
  dplyr::select(`Tumor line` = line, Analyte = analyte, `Time (day)` = time,
    `Simulated (nM)` = conc, `Figure 4A line (nM)` = paper, `Simulated / paper` = ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Simulated versus the digitized Figure 4A fitted lines.")
r_of <- function(ln, an) ratio$ratio[ratio$line == ln & ratio$analyte == an]
stopifnot(
  # GFP-MCF7 mice, whose small HER2 sink leaves plasma closest to the
  # plasma-only fit the paper plots: total trastuzumab and total MMAE within
  # 30% at 3 and 7 days. A wrong clearance, volume, deconjugation rate or
  # initial DAR moves at least one of them by far more.
  all(abs(log(r_of("GFP-MCF7", "Total trastuzumab"))) < log(1.3)),
  all(abs(log(r_of("GFP-MCF7", "Total MMAE"))) < log(1.3)),
  # N87 mice: the tumor HER2 sink lowers plasma exposure (envelope check).
  all(abs(log(r_of("N87", "Total trastuzumab"))) < log(1.5)),
  # Unconjugated MMAE at 3 days (formation-rate limited), both lines.
  all(abs(log(ratio$ratio[ratio$analyte == "Unconjugated MMAE" & ratio$time == 3])) < log(1.3))
)
```

The plasma profiles of GFP-MCF7 mice reproduce the paper's fitted lines. In N87
mice the larger tumor HER2 sink, which the full model carries, lowers plasma
total trastuzumab and total MMAE by 20-50 % at 7 days; the paper's Figure 4A
lines come from the plasma model fitted before the tumor was added and are
drawn once for both lines. Unconjugated MMAE at 7 days is about twice the
paper's line (0.065 versus 0.034 nM); the line declines more steeply than its
two-compartment MMAE parameters give when MMAE is formed from the ADC, which
the maintainers could not resolve from the printed equations.

```{r fig4bc, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4B-C of Singh 2019: tumor total trastuzumab, unconjugated MMAE and total MMAE (nM over the whole tumor volume) after 10 mg/kg. Points are the paper's tumor data at 1, 3 and 7 days, digitized by the maintainers from the low-resolution figure."}
tumor_long <- pk |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  dplyr::select(line, time,
    `Total trastuzumab` = tumor_total_trastuzumab,
    `Unconjugated MMAE` = tumor_free_mmae,
    `Total MMAE` = tumor_total_mmae
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(line, time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc")
fig4bc_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~line, ~analyte, ~time, ~conc,
  "GFP-MCF7", "Total trastuzumab", 1, 7, "GFP-MCF7", "Total trastuzumab", 3, 5,
  "GFP-MCF7", "Total trastuzumab", 7, 1.2,
  "GFP-MCF7", "Unconjugated MMAE", 1, 180, "GFP-MCF7", "Unconjugated MMAE", 3, 220,
  "GFP-MCF7", "Unconjugated MMAE", 7, 180,
  "GFP-MCF7", "Total MMAE", 1, 380, "GFP-MCF7", "Total MMAE", 3, 290,
  "GFP-MCF7", "Total MMAE", 7, 160,
  "N87", "Total trastuzumab", 1, 85, "N87", "Total trastuzumab", 3, 55,
  "N87", "Total trastuzumab", 7, 6,
  "N87", "Unconjugated MMAE", 1, 320, "N87", "Unconjugated MMAE", 3, 400,
  "N87", "Unconjugated MMAE", 7, 150,
  "N87", "Total MMAE", 1, 700, "N87", "Total MMAE", 3, 550,
  "N87", "Total MMAE", 7, 180
)
ggplot(tumor_long, aes(time, conc, colour = line)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig4bc_ref, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("GFP-MCF7" = "forestgreen", N87 = "red")) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumor concentration (nM)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Tumor unconjugated and total MMAE, and N87 total trastuzumab, follow the paper's
data. GFP-MCF7 total trastuzumab is several-fold above the paper's data and
fitted line (see the deviations section): with the printed exchange constants
the unbound ADC in the tumor extracellular space approaches the void fraction
times the plasma ADC concentration in both tumor lines, which caps how far the
GFP-MCF7 tumor can fall below the N87 tumor.

# Intracellular tubulin occupancy (Figure 5)

```{r occ-sim}
occ_times <- seq(0, 40, by = 0.1)
dose_grid <- c(1, 3, 5, 10)
occ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(0, 1), function(n87) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(dose_grid, function(dd) {
    solve_typ(dd, n87, 400, occ_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(dose = paste(dd, "mg/kg"), line = line_lab(n87))
  }))
}))
occ$dose <- factor(occ$dose, levels = paste(dose_grid, "mg/kg"))
```

```{r fig5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Singh 2019: simulated intracellular tubulin occupancy by MMAE after single IV doses of 1-10 mg/kg (typical values, no TGI feedback needed at this scale)."}
ggplot(occ, aes(time, tubulin_occupancy, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~line) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "% tubulin occupancy", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig5-check}
occ_peak <- occ |>
  dplyr::group_by(line, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim_peak = max(tubulin_occupancy), .groups = "drop")
# Peaks digitized by the maintainers from Figure 5.
occ_peak$paper_peak <- c(64.4, 80.1, 86.4, 92.3, 94, 97, 98, 98)
occ_peak |>
  dplyr::rename(`Tumor line` = line, Dose = dose, `Simulated peak (%)` = sim_peak,
    `Figure 5 peak (%)` = paper_peak) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  # Peak occupancy within 6 percentage points of Figure 5 in every arm. The
  # occupancy chain runs through the per-cell volume, SF, the tubulin unit
  # conversion and the HER2 counts; an error in any of them shifts the
  # GFP-MCF7 peaks by tens of points.
  all(abs(occ_peak$sim_peak - occ_peak$paper_peak) < 6),
  # Dose ordering of Figure 5 within each tumor line.
  all(tapply(occ_peak$sim_peak, occ_peak$line, function(x) all(diff(x) > 0)))
)
```

# Tumor growth inhibition (Figure 6)

```{r tgi-typ}
tgi_times <- seq(0, 60, by = 0.5)
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~line, ~n87, ~mgkg, ~tv0,
  "GFP-MCF7", 0, 0, 480, "GFP-MCF7", 0, 3, 450, "GFP-MCF7", 0, 5, 380, "GFP-MCF7", 0, 10, 450,
  "N87", 1, 0, 330, "N87", 1, 1, 380, "N87", 1, 3, 400, "N87", 1, 10, 420
)
tgi_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  solve_typ(arms$mgkg[i], arms$n87[i], arms$tv0[i], tgi_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(line = arms$line[i], arm = paste(arms$mgkg[i], "mg/kg"))
}))
```

```{r tgi-vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190225)
n_per_arm <- 100L
tgi_vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  ev <- make_events(arms$mgkg[i], arms$n87[i], arms$tv0[i], seq(0, 60, by = 1),
    n_id = n_per_arm
  )
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(line = arms$line[i], arm = paste(arms$mgkg[i], "mg/kg"))
})) |>
  dplyr::group_by(line, arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = stats::quantile(tumor_volume, 0.05),
    med = stats::median(tumor_volume),
    hi = stats::quantile(tumor_volume, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig6, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6 of Singh 2019: tumor volume after a single IV dose (line: typical value; band: 5th-95th percentile of 100 simulated mice per arm with the between-mouse variability on Kmax and tau). Initial volumes are read from Figure 6."}
arm_levels <- c("0 mg/kg", "1 mg/kg", "3 mg/kg", "5 mg/kg", "10 mg/kg")
ggplot(
  tgi_vpc |> dplyr::mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels)),
  aes(time)
) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(
    data = tgi_typ |> dplyr::mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels)),
    aes(y = tumor_volume, colour = line)
  ) +
  facet_grid(arm ~ line) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 3000)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("GFP-MCF7" = "forestgreen", N87 = "red"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = expression("Tumor volume (mm"^3 * ")")) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r tgi-check}
tv_at <- function(ln, a, t) tgi_typ$tumor_volume[tgi_typ$line == ln & tgi_typ$arm == a & tgi_typ$time == t]
stopifnot(
  # Untreated tumors double in their Table 1 doubling time (Eq 1); this pins
  # the 0.693 / DT growth rate and the tumor1 initial condition.
  abs(tv_at("GFP-MCF7", "0 mg/kg", 10.5) / 480 - 2^(10.5 / 10.6)) < 0.01,
  abs(tv_at("N87", "0 mg/kg", 13.5) / 330 - 2^(13.5 / 13.5)) < 0.01,
  # 10 mg/kg regresses N87 tumors almost completely (Figure 6 B4).
  tv_at("N87", "10 mg/kg", 20) < 0.15 * 420,
  # GFP-MCF7 at 10 mg/kg is held near its starting volume for about 3 weeks
  # (Figure 6 A4).
  tv_at("GFP-MCF7", "10 mg/kg", 20) < 1.2 * 450,
  # Dose ordering at day 20 in both lines.
  all(diff(sapply(c("0 mg/kg", "3 mg/kg", "5 mg/kg", "10 mg/kg"), function(a) tv_at("GFP-MCF7", a, 20))) < 0),
  all(diff(sapply(c("0 mg/kg", "1 mg/kg", "3 mg/kg", "10 mg/kg"), function(a) tv_at("N87", a, 20))) < 0)
)
```

The controls, GFP-MCF7 at 3 mg/kg and the complete N87 regression at 10 mg/kg
match Figure 6. Regrowth after GFP-MCF7 5 and 10 mg/kg comes roughly a week
earlier than the paper's fitted lines, and N87 tumors at 1 and 3 mg/kg shrink
more than the paper shows. With a sigmoidicity of 15 and a KC50 of 96.8 %, the
kill rate exceeds the N87 growth rate for any occupancy above about 85 %, and
Figure 5 itself shows N87 occupancy above 85 % for several days after 1 mg/kg;
the printed Table 1 kill parameters and the Figure 5 occupancies therefore
predict a stronger low-dose N87 effect than Figure 6 displays. The parameters
are kept as printed.

# NCA comparison

The paper reports non-compartmental half-lives from its observed plasma and
tumor data (Section 4.1) and tumor AUC(0-7 d) ratios between the two lines.
PKNCA is run on the typical-value profiles sampled at the study times
(10 min, 1, 3 and 7 days).

```{r pknca}
nca_times <- c(0, 10 / 1440, 1, 3, 7)
nca_src <- pk |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% nca_times) |>
  dplyr::select(line, time,
    plasma_total_trastuzumab = Cc,
    plasma_total_mmae, plasma_free_mmae,
    tumor_total_trastuzumab, tumor_free_mmae, tumor_total_mmae
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(line, time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = paste(line, analyte, sep = " | ")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc))
dose_df <- nca_src |>
  dplyr::distinct(treatment, id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, dose = dose_nmol(10))
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_src, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
# Half-lives for the plasma analytes (falling over 1-7 days); AUC(0-7 d) for
# the tumor analytes, whose 1-7 day samples include the plateau.
nca_intervals <- dplyr::distinct(nca_src, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    start = 0, end = 7,
    half.life = grepl("plasma", treatment),
    auclast = grepl("tumor", treatment)
  )
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = as.data.frame(nca_intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data))
```

```{r nca-table}
sim_hl <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
ref_hl <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~half.life,
  "GFP-MCF7 | plasma_total_trastuzumab", 1.4,
  "N87 | plasma_total_trastuzumab", 1.2,
  "GFP-MCF7 | plasma_total_mmae", 0.9,
  "N87 | plasma_total_mmae", 0.8,
  "GFP-MCF7 | plasma_free_mmae", 1.07,
  "N87 | plasma_free_mmae", 1.14
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_hl,
  reference = ref_hl,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "day")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Half-lives: Section 4.1 of Singh 2019 (NCA of observed data) versus PKNCA on the simulated typical profiles.")
attr(cmp, "footnote")
```

```{r auc-ratio}
auc <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", grepl("^tumor", sub(".*\\| ", "", treatment))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    line = sub(" \\|.*", "", treatment),
    analyte = sub(".*\\| ", "", treatment)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(line, analyte, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = line, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_ratio = N87 / `GFP-MCF7`)
auc$paper_ratio <- c(
  tumor_total_trastuzumab = 12, tumor_free_mmae = 1.6, tumor_total_mmae = 1.8
)[auc$analyte]
auc |>
  dplyr::select(Analyte = analyte, `Simulated N87/MCF7` = sim_ratio, `Paper N87/MCF7` = paper_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Tumor AUC(0-7 d) ratio, N87 over GFP-MCF7 (Section 4.1).")
stopifnot(
  # N87 tumors see more of every analyte than GFP-MCF7 tumors, and the MMAE
  # ratios stay small (saturable tubulin binding caps intracellular MMAE).
  all(auc$sim_ratio > 1),
  all(auc$sim_ratio[auc$analyte != "tumor_total_trastuzumab"] < 2)
)
# Tumor MMAE concentrations against the digitized Figure 4B-C data, both lines,
# 1-7 days.
mmae_cmp <- tumor_long |>
  dplyr::filter(analyte != "Total trastuzumab") |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = round(time, 6)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    fig4bc_ref |> dplyr::rename(paper = conc),
    by = c("line", "analyte", "time")
  )
stopifnot(
  abs(stats::median(log(mmae_cmp$conc / mmae_cmp$paper))) < log(1.3),
  all(abs(log(mmae_cmp$conc / mmae_cmp$paper)) < log(2))
)
```

Plasma total and unconjugated MMAE half-lives agree with the paper. The total
trastuzumab half-lives in the paper come from three mice per time point and
are shorter than its own fitted plasma line, which falls from about 214 to
82 nM between days 3 and 7 (a 2.9-day half-life); the simulation follows the
fitted line. The tumor half-lives of total trastuzumab (2.14 and 1.58 days)
cannot be estimated from three post-peak samples on the typical profile and
are not compared.

Tumor MMAE concentrations agree with the paper's data within a factor of 2 at
every sampled time, but the simulated N87/GFP-MCF7 exposure ratios (about 1.1)
are smaller than the paper's 1.6-1.8 because simulated GFP-MCF7 MMAE runs above
the data at 1-3 days. The total-trastuzumab ratio is the GFP-MCF7 discrepancy
discussed under Figure 4.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Cell volume and SF are taken from the single-cell source.** Equations 9 and
  12 use the volume of one tumor cell (VCell) and a molecule-to-nmol scaling
  factor (SF), neither of which the 2019 paper prints. Both come from Table 2
  of Singh and Shah 2017 (Drug Metab Dispos 45:1120): VCell = 3.12 pL (N87) and
  8.14 pL (GFP-MCF7), SF = 10^9 / 6.023e23. Following that paper, tubulin
  (65 nM) and its association rate (1/nM/h) are converted to molecules per cell
  with VCell and SF, which puts Equations 12-14 on consistent units.
* **Tumor exchange in Equation 5 is mass-balanced.** The printed Equation 5
  subtracts the plasma-to-tumor MMAE flux as a concentration rate without the
  tumor-volume / V1Drug factor that Equation 23 uses for the matching tumor
  gain (and that Equation 3 uses for the ADC). The model scales the term by
  `tv / vc_mmae`. As printed, plasma unconjugated MMAE at 7 days would be
  about 0.59 nM, against 0.034 nM on the paper's fitted line; the
  mass-balanced form gives 0.065 nM.
* **Plasma total trastuzumab includes deconjugated antibody.** Equation 3
  removes deconjugated antibody from the ADC state, but the paper's fitted
  total-trastuzumab line in Figure 4A (about 740, 214 and 82 nM at 0, 3 and
  7 days) declines like ADC plus the antibody left behind by deconjugation,
  cleared with the ADC parameters (simulated: 794, 210 and 85 nM), whereas the
  ADC state alone falls to 21 nM by day 7. The model therefore carries that
  antibody in plasma (`mab_central`, `mab_peripheral`) for the `Cc` output
  only; it does not enter the tumor. The ADC state alone is output as
  `plasma_adc`, and total MMAE uses the ADC state times the DAR, which matches
  the paper's total-MMAE line.
* **Tumor output definitions are inferred.** The paper does not write the
  observation equations. Tumor total trastuzumab is extracellular ADC plus
  HER2-bound and internalized ADC; unconjugated MMAE is extracellular plus
  cytoplasmic plus tubulin-bound MMAE; total MMAE adds the conjugated payload
  (tumor total trastuzumab times the DAR). All are nM over the whole tumor
  volume.
* **GFP-MCF7 tumor total trastuzumab is not reproduced.** It is several-fold
  above the paper's data and line, and the N87/GFP-MCF7 AUC ratio is about 1.4
  rather than 12. N87 total trastuzumab and both MMAE analytes in both tumors
  are within a factor of 2 of the data. No reading of the printed equations that the maintainers tried
  removes the extracellular unbound ADC that dominates the GFP-MCF7 signal.
* **TGI.** Low-dose N87 tumors shrink more, and treated GFP-MCF7 tumors regrow
  earlier, than in Figure 6 (see the Figure 6 section). No parameter was
  adjusted.
* **Number of cells.** NC = 10^5 cells per mm^3 of total tumor volume (all four
  transit compartments, since cellular processing continues in non-growing
  cells, Section 2.7.5), from the 10^8 cells/g assumption and the 10^5 factor in
  Equations 22-23.
* **Body weight and ADC molecular weight.** Table 1 PK parameters are per kg,
  while Equation 3 exchanges whole-tumor amounts with the central compartment,
  so the model scales clearances and volumes by `WT`. Weight is not reported;
  25 g is assumed here. Doses use 150,000 g/mol for the ADC.
* **Initial DAR.** Set to 4 from the 'average DAR of ~4' in Section 2.2; the
  single-cell source measured 4.5 for its own batch.
* **Between-mouse variability.** Table 1 reports IIVKmax and IIVtau as
  percentages (10.16 and 19.4) with RSEs in parentheses; they are read as the
  Monolix omega (standard deviation of the log-normal random effect) times 100.
* **Residual error.** Neither the ADAPT variance-model coefficients (Equation 24)
  nor the Monolix TGI error model are reported; both residual SDs are fixed to
  zero.
* **Units.** Time is in days throughout; the per-hour single-cell constants of
  Table 1 are multiplied by 24 inside the model.
